result.final_message:
I built the Everbloom app in UIKit and checked every item on the "Done" list in the iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2). A physical iPhone wasn't available, and the signed device build (with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set) was never run.

**What I checked**
- **Builds:** both commands in `BUILD.md` succeed from an empty `build/` folder: the device Release build with signing disabled (a 928 KB `.app`) and the simulator Release build.
- **Flows:** I added an XCUITest target (`EverbloomUITests`, not part of the app) and all four of its tests pass:
  - Home loads, a collection scrolls to its end, and all four sorts work.
  - Search returns results and scrolls.
  - A product opens, options switch, and a recommendation opens another product.
  - Add to cart switches to Cart and updates the badge. The stepper changes the subtotal, and going to 0 shows the empty cart. Check out opens the checkout page in an in-app browser.
- **Error state:** pointed at a local port with nothing listening, Home shows the error screen. After I started a small forwarding proxy on that port, Retry loaded the content.
- **Log marker:** `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears exactly once per launch in the simulator log stream, and the app logs nothing else.
- **Identifiers:** every identifier the flows touch was found, including the tabs and `cart-badge`. A few were set in code but never queried by a test (for example `product-card-<i>` and `search-result-<i>` cells).

**Two things that differ from what you might expect**
- **Tab bar look:** it uses the standard UIKit tab bar, which on iOS 26 and later is drawn as the floating "Liquid Glass" bar, not the flat bar in the mockup. I kept the platform default.
- **Cart badge:** UIKit's built-in badge can't carry an accessibility identifier, so the badge is my own label placed over the Cart tab, styled per the design. Its position comes from finding the tab buttons at runtime. That worked on this simulator but wasn't tested on other iOS versions.

**Smaller decisions** (all recorded in `NOTES.md`)
- There are no third-party dependencies; Check out uses Apple's own in-app browser.
- I left out the "See all" link drawn in the Home mockup, because the spec doesn't mention it.
- On the product I tested, both variants cost $75, so the test saw the selection change but not the price change.
- Stepper taps made while a cart request is still running are ignored.

The Xcode project is checked in, so building needs no extra tools. It was generated from `project.yml` with XcodeGen, which you only need if you edit `project.yml`.

Files are in `/Users/itome/shopbench-runs/uikit`:
- `Everbloom/`
- `EverbloomUITests/`
- `Everbloom.xcodeproj`
- `project.yml`
- `BUILD.md`
- `NOTES.md`

interventions.message: On a physical iPhone 12 (iOS 27.2, the signed device release build), with SHOP_API_URL pointing at a replay server on the local network that answers within a few milliseconds, the app crashes every time a collection is opened from Home. The crash report shows an NSInternalInconsistencyException raised by UICollectionView (_Bug_Detected_In_Client_Of_UICollectionView_Invalid_Batch_Updates) from performBatchUpdates in CollectionViewController.apply(_:), called from the closure in CollectionViewController.load(reset:). Fix the crash.

result.final_message:
I fixed the crash. I reproduced it in the simulator using a local replay server that answers in milliseconds, and the same crash no longer happens there. I haven't run it on a physical iPhone.

**Cause.** When the first page of products arrived, the code asked the grid to reload, but UIKit postpones that reload until the next screen update. The "load more near the end" check ran in between and measured the grid while it still looked empty. So it requested page 2 straight away. With a fast server, page 2 arrived before the screen update: the grid still thought it had 0 items while the data reported 48. Inserting 24 items into that mismatch is the invalid update in your crash report. Slow networks always left time for the screen to update between pages, which is why it didn't show up earlier.

**Fix** (in `Everbloom/CollectionViewController.swift`):
- **Data source:** the grid now uses UIKit's diffable data source (`UICollectionViewDiffableDataSource`). UIKit then keeps the grid's item count in step with the data itself, so the mismatch can't happen however fast pages arrive. Each item is identified by its list position plus the current sort order, so changing the sort refreshes the cards.
- **Load-more check:** it now finishes laying out the grid before measuring. It also runs once when the screen appears. Page 2 is no longer fetched until the user actually scrolls near the end; in the replay test, only 12 of 48 collection requests asked for a later page.
- **Search:** it had the same pattern on its list. I applied the same load-more fix there, and it checks the list's row count before inserting.

**Testing.** I added two UI tests that open and scroll several collections, change the sort, and run searches against the replay server on `127.0.0.1:8787`. Before the fix, the collection test crashed in `CollectionViewController.apply(_:)`, both with an empty cache and with a warm one. After the fix it passed twice in a row, the second time with every response served from cache, and the new search test passed both times. The full set of six UI tests passes, and the device release build still compiles with signing disabled.

`NOTES.md` and `BUILD.md` are updated, including how to run the new tests.
